Measure quantitative serum beta-hCG + perform pelvic ultrasonography

**Beta-hCG below discriminatory zone:** repeat beta-hCG and ultrasound in 48 hours
Assess hemodynamic stability + check for peritoneal signs or tubal rupture

**Stable + unruptured + hCG < 5000 + no fetal cardiac activity:** administer intramuscular methotrexate

algorithm.title: Calculation of attributable risk and relative risk in cohort studies

nodes.text: Recognize epidemiological risk measures in prospective cohort studies
Calculate incidence rate in exposed group (Ie): 30 / 1000 = 0.030 (3.0%)
Calculate incidence rate in unexposed group (Iu): 3 / 1000 = 0.003 (0.3%)
Calculate Attributable Risk (AR = Risk Difference): AR = Ie - Iu = 0.030 - 0.003 = 0.027 (2.7%)
**Attributable risk percent (ARP):** ARP = (Ie - Iu) / Ie = 0.027 / 0.030 = 90%
**Relative risk (RR):** RR = Ie / Iu = 0.030 / 0.003 = 10.0
Interpret attributable risk as excess disease incidence directly attributable to the exposure

Calculate absolute risk in unexposed: 500 cases / 1000 subjects = 0.50

algorithm.title: Calculation of absolute risk reduction and number needed to treat

nodes.text: Identify baseline event rate in control group (CER): standard care mortality = 15% (0.15)
Identify experimental event rate (EER): RPM group mortality = 13% (0.13)
Calculate Absolute Risk Reduction (ARR): ARR = CER - EER = 0.15 - 0.13 = 0.02 (2%)
Calculate Number Needed to Treat (NNT): NNT = 1 / ARR = 1 / 0.02 = 50
**Rounding rule for clinical practice:** always round NNT up to the next integer
Do not confuse with Relative Risk Reduction (RRR): RRR = ARR / CER = 0.02 / 0.15
